Finding out what is there

Asbestos inspections and testing, before anything is disturbed

Identification and sampling of suspected asbestos before demolition or renovation. Samples are analysed by an accredited laboratory, and the result is what turns a guess about the scope into a quantity somebody can price and plan around. Send the address and the age of the building, and we will arrange sampling before any work begins.

0456 220 552

Removal by licensed asbestos removalists. Max holds demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Decide what is being disturbed

    Who You, with your builder or us

    The survey covers what the work will touch. A scope that changes later means a survey that has to be extended.

  2. 02

    Access to every area

    Who You

    Subfloor, roof space, wet areas and behind linings. An area that cannot be reached is an area that has to be presumed to contain asbestos.

  3. 03

    Sampling by a competent person

    Who Max, through the accredited laboratory

    Samples taken under controlled conditions. Taking your own sample disturbs the material you were trying to assess.

  4. 04

    Laboratory analysis

    Who Accredited laboratory

    The analysis is what makes the result usable. A visual opinion is not a result.

  5. 05

    Written report

    Who The laboratory and the assessor

    Material, location, type and condition. This is what the removalist quotes from and what the demolisher plans around.

  6. 06

    Decision on scope

    Who You, with the report in hand

    What gets removed, in what order, and under which licence class.

The detail

Why the survey is the cheapest step on the job

  • It converts a range into a number. Without it, every removal quote carries a contingency, and you pay for that contingency whether the asbestos is there or not.
  • It sets the licence class. Bonded and friable are different licences, different controls and very different costs. Which one you need is a laboratory answer.
  • It protects the programme. Asbestos found after demolition has started stops the job. That is the single most common reason a knockdown runs late.
  • It protects the ground. Material broken up before it was identified contaminates the soil you were about to build on, and soil remediation costs far more than a survey.
  • It is required before the work, not after. Anything built before 1990 is presumed to contain asbestos until testing shows otherwise.
  • It stays useful. The report is what the removalist quotes from, what the demolisher plans around, and what you hand over at the end.

What we need to quote it

The address
So we can look at access and what is around it
Photographs
One from the street and one of the work itself
Any reports you hold
Hazardous materials, structural, survey or levels
Your dates
What has to be finished by when, and what is waiting on it

We attend the site before quoting anything substantial.

If it was built before 1990, assume it is there

Eaves, fibro sheeting, wet area linings, vinyl floor tiles, roof sheets and fencing are all common in Australian housing stock of that age. Testing is what tells you which of them apply to your property.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

Can I take my own sample?
We would strongly advise against it. Breaking a piece off the material you suspect is exactly the action that releases fibres, and an untrained sample taken without controls is both a risk and usually not accepted by a laboratory anyway.
How long does the result take?
The site work is usually a few hours. The laboratory turnaround is the part that sets the timeline, and it is worth starting the survey the day you have approval rather than the week before you want a machine on site.
What if an area cannot be accessed?
It is presumed to contain asbestos and noted as presumed rather than tested. That is the honest result. If the presumption is expensive, opening the area up for access is usually cheaper than carrying it.
Does a clear result mean the whole property is clear?
It means the sampled materials within the scope are clear. If the scope later widens, the survey has to widen with it.
Do I need this if I am only renovating?
If the renovation disturbs linings, ceilings, floor coverings, eaves or wet areas in a pre 1990 building, yes. Those are precisely where bonded asbestos sits.

Get a quote

Send a photograph and the age of the building

A picture of the material and roughly when the building went up is usually enough to tell you whether it needs testing. We will tell you honestly either way.
